question: Belgian fruit growers use pesticides such as Spirotetramat1 to protect their crops. Due to recent developments in the new directive on endocrine disruptors, the producer of Movento/Batavia (Bayer) has decided not to submit a renewal application for its product to the EU.

To meet the requirements of the new directive, additional research work was done to understand better the mechanism of the known effects of Spirotetramat. While some results led to clear assessments ruling out any mechanism of action of endocrine disruptors, other study results were inconclusive.
Partly because of this uncertainty, the manufacturer decided to discontinue the product and it will no longer be available in the EU from 20252. 1.
Can the Commission provide more information on possible alternatives being explored to meet pest control needs after the above-mentioned discontinuation owing to EU legislation?
Are there any plans to introduce new, innovative pest control products on the EU market, and if so, what are they?

What studies were carried out to assess the effects of Spirotetramat with regard to EU legislation on endocrine disruptors, and can the Commission provide further insight into the findings of these studies and how they contributed to the decision-making process?
Marketed under the brand names Movento and Batavia The product remains available in other parts of the world.
answer: As the Honourable Member stated, the approval of spirotetramat expires on 30 April 2024. This is because no applicant has submitted an application for the renewal of its approval. Several other active substances, chemicals or microorganisms, which can be used in plant protection products (PPPs) to control the same kind of pests in fruit crops are approved.

PPPs containing other active substances and authorised for similar uses in Belgium can be found in the official Belgian database Fytoweb (3). Further new active substances are being assessed by Member States, before their peer-review coordinated by the European Food Safety Authority and subsequent approval, if safe uses are demonstrated.

Such new active substances also include innovations like peptides, Ribonucleic acid interference (RNAi) substances, or bacteriophages. Moreover, research and innovation enabling sustainable plant protection and innovative pest contro l (4) are funded under the EU Research Framework Programmes, Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe (5).

The Commission is not aware of the studies carried out by the applicant, pursuant to Regulation (EC) 1107/2009 (6), to assess the potential endocrine disrupting effects of spirotetramat. The decision not to submit an application for renewal of approval was made solely by the company.
